left_defects.translation: the 82-year-old man, deprived of his censorship

right_defects.translation: a man brought into suspicion by many (a) because of his reputation
slanders and exiles with equal zeal and patience (h) [note (i) dropped]

why: Each side has one real mistranslation near the break (left before it, right after it) of similar weight.
Both render the stockings/gloves entry and the entry/exit fees across the break completely and correctly.

left_defects.source: sie meiner nicht Macht und Gewalt, sondern Geist und Krafft
left_defects.translation: not by my power and might, but by Spirit and strength

why: Left misreads the ungueltig clause after the break and the Magnificat gloss before it; right renders both plausibly.

right_defects.source: Damna- / mnatur ab Episcopis haec instructio
right_defects.translation: They condemn- / this instruction is condemned by the bishops

why: Right garbles the hyphenated damnatur into a dangling active verb plus a restated sentence; left joins it cleanly.

right_defects.translation: in the Gallic Churches on account of Ubiquity. (repeated after the break)

right_defects.source: quam Osiander tanquam non satis synceram, alij autem ... etiam velut erroneam anathematizant
right_defects.translation: which Osiander anathematizes as not sufficiently sincere

why: Right repeats the pre-break clause after the break and misassigns the anathema to Osiander.

left_defects.translation: friends of J.B. whom I have known

why: Left stutters Greek across the catchword and adds a clause; right mistranslates mit Fleiss (deliberately) and leaves a term untranslated, comparable weight.
